newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steadied by crude, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steadied by crude, trade quiet.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, helped by firmer crude, held relatively steady Monday, but trade remained light ahead of the New Year's Day holiday Wednesday, industry sources said.
But with gas prices cratering and milder weather on the horizon, some saw selling pressure ahead.

"It's still too early to write off winter, but these gas prices are going to put pressure on fuel oil sellers to lower their numbers," said one East Coast utility source, referring to the more than 30 percent slide in NYMEX gas prices in the last five sessions.

In New York Harbor, one percent held steady at $21.00-25 a barrel, with January one percent paper also little changed at $20.25-50, traders said. Feb one percent paper was quoted steady to up slightly at $19.75-20.00.
High sulphurs in New York also notionally were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, prices also were stable from Friday, with one percent still at $18.75 and three percent at $16.25-50, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices tumbled more than 50 cents Monday to about the $3.45-3.50/mmBtu level, almost competitive with NYH one percent resid at a $3.35/mmBtu equivalent.
